identity.note: RFC 2606 reserves .invalid permanently, so this namespace can never correspond to a real host. Every uuid below is uuid5(namespace, label) and is therefore reproducible from this file alone (SEC-011 / AC-059).

accept_boundary_200.note: Exactly 200 records: one page filled to the API maximum limit. The terminal page is FULL, so a reader that stops only on a short page loops forever here.

accept_boundary_201.note: 201 records: the first record past the limit, so page two holds exactly one.

accept_empty_collection.note: A genuinely empty collection: count == 0 AND totalCount == 0, which DATA-009b makes a COMPLETE result. The empty site is exactly the site whose owner is setting the plugin up for the first time.

accept_single_page_25.note: 25 records: one page, at the >25 default-limit boundary.

advance_by_validated_count.note: The response echoes a limit of four when two was requested. Advancing by response arithmetic rather than the validated count skips records.

count_within_limit.note: A page returns three records for a limit of two.

empty_is_valid_not_premature.note: count == 0 while offset < totalCount. Read together with accept_empty_collection this pair is the whole of DATA-009b; either one alone can be satisfied by a wrong rule.

max_decoded_bytes_enforced.note: Pages whose accumulated decoded size crosses the 8 MiB per-collection bound before the page count does. Synthesized, as above.

max_pages_enforced.note: 65 pages: one past the 64-page bound. A controller that never reports a terminal page must not hang the batch. Synthesized rather than committed — materialising it is 6 MB of near-identical records in a repository that gets cloned into the plugins directory on install.

non_terminal_page_progresses.note: A middle page is empty while offset < totalCount: premature, and the deliberate twin of accept_empty_collection.

offset_matches_request.note: Page 2 answers with offset 1 for a request at offset 2.

record_ids_unique.note: Two records on one page share an id, so accumulation reaches four unique records for a totalCount of five and never terminates.

reread_page_zero_matches.note: OFFSET DRIFT AT CONSTANT CARDINALITY. One record is deleted and another appended after page 0 is read, so every later page slides by one and exactly one record is never returned. Offsets, counts, id uniqueness, totalCount stability and terminal completeness ALL still pass. The trailing response is the DATA-009a re-read of page 0, which is the only thing in the contract that catches this.

terminal_completeness.note: The collection terminates on a short page with fewer unique records accumulated than the terminal totalCount claims: 3 against 5.

total_count_stable.note: totalCount changes between the first page and the last.

all-down.note: Every gateway down. REQ-002 rule 3 (red), which strictly precedes amber.

all-states.note: One device in each of the ten API states plus REBOOTING, which is outside the enum and must land in `unknown` with a warning (REQ-000).
all-states.schemaDeviation: device.state enum relaxed: REBOOTING is deliberately outside the published enum, because REQ-000's `unknown` class has no other way to be exercised.

console-without-gateway-feature.note: DEV-6: no device advertises `gateway`, and the console is identified by reporting a global address. wan.status == up with the console's metrics, counts.gateways == 1, and the role rows over-count (REQ-009).

degraded.note: One down, one impaired, one transitional. REQ-002 rule 4 (amber); the UPDATING AP must NOT contribute.

empty-site.note: Zero adopted devices. REQ-002 rule 2 (grey) and UX-005; the page is a VALID empty result, not a premature one (DATA-009b).

five-gateways.note: Five gateways: statistics are fetched for at most four (REQ-008a), the fifth listed without metrics plus a warning.

healthy.note: Every device online, one gateway. REQ-002 rule 5 (green).

large-500-down.note: 500 devices, every one down. Three pages at limit 200; the envelope bounds offlineDevices to 10 while offlineTotal stays 500, which is what AC-063's "and 490 more" is computed from.

multi-feature.note: A Dream Machine reporting all three roles at once, an AP-only device, and a device with an EMPTY features array. byClass must count all three exactly once; the role objects must not sum to devicesTotal.

multi-site.note: Several sites and no committed siteId: DATA-012 requires site_unselected with the {id, name} pairs carried in warnings.

no-gateway.note: No gateway-featured device: can never be red (rule 3 needs one) and reports wan.status == unknown.

two-gateways.note: One ONLINE, one ISOLATED: amber via rule 4, NOT red, and wan.status == degraded.

zero-site.note: Zero sites: DATA-012 requires `unsupported`, not an empty success.
